I.imaging: subcapsular hematoma <10% surface area; capsular tear <1 cm depth

II.imaging: subcapsular hematoma 10-50% surface; laceration 1-3 cm depth, <10 cm length

III.imaging: subcapsular hematoma >50% or expanding; laceration >3 cm depth; any vascular injury

IV.imaging: parenchymal disruption 25-75% of a hepatic lobe; active bleeding within parenchyma

V.imaging: parenchymal disruption >75% of a lobe; juxtahepatic venous injury; active bleeding beyond parenchyma into peritoneum

II.imaging: subcapsular hematoma 10-50% surface; laceration 1-3 cm depth not involving trabecular vessels

III.imaging: subcapsular hematoma >50% or expanding; laceration >3 cm depth or involving trabecular vessels

IV.imaging: any injury with vascular involvement and active bleeding confined within capsule; >25% devascularization

V.imaging: shattered spleen; vascular hilar injury with devascularization; active bleeding beyond capsule

I.imaging: subcapsular hematoma without parenchymal laceration; contusion

II.imaging: perirenal hematoma confined to retroperitoneum; laceration <1 cm depth without urinary extravasation

III.imaging: laceration >1 cm depth without collecting-system rupture or urinary extravasation

IV.imaging: laceration through cortex, medulla and collecting system; segmental vascular injury; urinary extravasation

V.imaging: shattered kidney; main renal artery or vein laceration; devascularized kidney
